name: Act of September 1, 1888 ratifying the agreement of May 27, 1887 for the Pocatello townsite on the Fort Hall Reservation
nations: Shoshone-Bannock Tribes of the Fort Hall Reservation
promises: The Shoshone and Bannack gave up about 1,840 acres in Township 6 South, Range 34 East, to be laid out as a townsite and sold at public auction after appraisal (Article I).
The proceeds, after the costs of survey, appraisal and sale, would be deposited in the Treasury to the Indians' credit at five per cent interest (Article I).
All unexecuted provisions of existing treaties not affected by the agreement would remain in force (Article III).
today: The Act records the agreement as signed by a majority of adult men as article 11 of the 1868 treaty required. No finding about the townsite sale was located; the 1968 Commission settlement of the Fort Hall dockets covered the 1889 and 1898 cessions and other claims, not this one.

sources.title: Act of September 1, 1888, ch. 936, 25 Stat. 452
sources.publisher: US Government Publishing Office (Statutes at Large)

Shoshone-Bannock Tribes et al. v. United States, Dockets 326-D to 326-H, 366, 367, Findings of Fact on Settlement, 19 Ind. Cl. Comm. 3 (February 13, 1968)

openQuestions: treaties.json lists Coeur d'Alene among the schedule tribes and repeats the Shoshone-Bannock Tribes twice; Royce and the Act name only the Shoshone and Bannock of Fort Hall.

The Act's preamble states the Utah and Northern Railroad had run through the reservation since about 1878 without paying the Indians anything for the land; that right of way belongs to a separate record.
What the townsite lots sold for and whether the proceeds were credited were not found.
The Shoshone-Bannock Tribes' own account of the Pocatello cession was not located.
